bridge.description: Cross-framework correspondences (bridges_to, corresponds_to, translates_to, compares_with, orthodox_target, mathlib_target).

construction.description: Constructive/derivational relations (depends_on, uses, constructs, derives, proves, assumes, requires, extends, refines).

evidence.description: Empirical / validation relations (supports, constrains, falsifies, tested_by, validated_by, challenged_by).

navigation.description: Reader-navigation pointers (part_of, has_part, next_step, previous_step, route, related_to, future_work, background_context, mentions, see_also).

projection.description: How items project into artifacts and surfaces (appears_in, published_in, formalized_by, implemented_by, represented_by, explained_in, summarized_by).

version.description: Version/lifecycle relations (replaces, supersedes, deprecated_by, retired_in, corrected_by, erratum_for).

predicates.description: This item depends on the target for its construction or proof.
This item makes use of the target (definition, lemma, theorem) in its content.
This item constructs the target object/structure.
This item derives the target via inference.
This item is a proof establishing the target theorem/lemma/proposition.
This item explicitly assumes the target (axiom, gate, hypothesis).
Stronger form of depends_on; the target must be discharged for this item to hold.
This item extends the target with additional structure.
This item refines the target (more precise statement, tighter hypothesis).
This item appears in (is rendered by) the target artifact (book, paper, dossier).
This item is published in the target venue/artifact.
This (prose) item has a formalization at the target (formal_theorem, formal_definition).
This item is implemented by the target (code, model, artifact).
This item is represented by the target page or projection surface.
The target provides exposition/explanation of this item.
The target provides a summary of this item.
This item summarizes the target (inverse of summarized_by; used by research notes summarizing a theorem).
This bridge_claim bridges to the target external/orthodox object.
This item corresponds to the target across a bridge.
This item translates to the target in a target framework/language.
This item compares with the target (informational).
Identifies the orthodox counterpart to a τ-side construction.
Identifies the Mathlib declaration this item targets.
This item replaces the target (newer version, same identity).
This item supersedes the target (non-equivalent successor; new CID).
This item has been deprecated by the target.
This item was retired in the target release.
This item has been corrected by the target erratum.
This erratum applies to the target.
This item supports the target (provides evidence/argument for it).
This item constrains the target.
This item falsifies the target.
This item is tested by the target (prediction, experiment, validation).
This item tests the target (inverse of tested_by; used by predictions/falsifiers/experiments).
This item is validated by the target (e.g., external review, audit, replication).
This item is challenged by the target (informational).
This item is part of the target (e.g., construction_step part_of construction).
This item has the target as a part.
Pointer to the next step in a sequence (e.g., construction spine).
Pointer to the previous step in a sequence.
A routing pointer between items in a multi-step navigation.
Proof step uses the target definition.
Proof step uses the target lemma.
Proof step uses the target theorem.
Proof step uses the target assumption / axiom.
Proof step uses the target bridge claim.
Proof step uses the target result.
Proof cites background context (not load-bearing).
Reference to a historical item (no current load-bearing role).
Generic "related to" link; informational only.
Item lists future work direction.
Background-context reference (not load-bearing).
Item mentions the target (no load-bearing role).
"See also" pointer.
